question: In Walter Murch's weighting of what a cut must serve, how much does continuity of space count?
answer: Four per cent. Murch's Rule of Six ranks emotion at 51%, story 23%, rhythm 10%, where the eye is looking 7%, the flat screen 5%, and three-dimensional space 4%. Emotion outweighs the other five combined, so an editor sacrifices from the bottom: a glass that jumps hands is forgiven when the moment lands.
move: When something must give, decide in advance which things are allowed to break.
source: Murch, In the Blink of an Eye
reference: Murch, In the Blink of an Eye: A Perspective on Film Editing, 2nd edn, Silman-James Press, 2001
